chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever sells a palm tree that has fruited, its fruit belongs to the seller, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.'
Then he said: 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled according to that.'

key_terms.قَضَى: He ruled / decreed (in a legal context)

ai.seo_question: Who owns the fruit of a palm tree after it is sold?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the default ownership of fruit on sold palm trees, establishing that produce remains with the seller unless explicitly stipulated otherwise by the buyer. It traces this legal precedent back to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who attributes it directly to the Prophet Muhammad, thereby reinforcing the continuity of Prophetic jurisprudence in commercial transactions. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on precise contractual stipulations (*shurut*) in sales to prevent disputes over natural yield.
